glossary.def: Real GitHub issues from popular Python repos. The model must write code that passes the existing test suite. "Verified" means a human checked that each issue is solvable. Scores range 0-100%.
Massive Multitask Language Understanding. 57 academic subjects from high-school to professional level (law, medicine, STEM). Tests breadth of knowledge. Scores are % correct.
OpenAI benchmark: 164 hand-crafted Python programming problems. Measures functional code generation (pass@1). Widely used but considered dated for frontier models.
Massive Multidisciplinary Multimodal Understanding. 11.5K questions requiring images (charts, diagrams, photos) plus text. Standard for vision-language model evaluation.
Ruler for Long-Context Evaluation. Tests retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, and aggregation over very long documents (up to 128K tokens). Better signal than "needle in haystack" for long-context claims.
Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A, Diamond split. Expert-level science questions that Google cannot directly answer. High signal for deep scientific reasoning. Human experts score ~65%.
Competition mathematics (AMC, AIME, Olympiad). 12,500 problems across 7 difficulty levels. Tests symbolic reasoning and multi-step derivation. Scores are % correct.

free-models.question: Are free AI models really free?
free-models.answer: Three kinds of free exist: open-weight models you self-host (free forever, you pay only infrastructure), permanent free API tiers (free within rate limits), and no-signup tools. The catch is usually rate limits, non-commercial clauses, or your data being used for training. Every listing here shows its catch.

free-models.question: What is the best free AI model right now?
free-models.answer: It depends on the job: the community votes on this page rank what practitioners actually rate highest, and you can filter by text, code, image, video, audio, or embeddings. For raw quality per dollar, open-weight frontier models you self-host are hard to beat.

free-models.question: Can I use free AI models commercially?
free-models.answer: Often yes for permissive open-weight licenses (Apache-2.0, MIT), but many free API tiers prohibit commercial use and some community licenses add revenue caps. Check the commercial column on each listing and verify the current license before shipping.

free-models.question: Do free AI API keys without signup exist?
free-models.answer: Yes, a small set of services work with no key at all, and they are labeled No-signup here. Never use shared API keys posted online: they run on someone else's billing, violate provider terms, and get revoked.

free-models.question: How do I use a free model in my own project?
free-models.answer: Most free API tiers are OpenAI-compatible, so you point your SDK at the provider base URL with your free key. Every listing has a How drawer with setup steps, a quickstart snippet, and a copy-paste prompt that walks Claude Code through the setup for you.

models--pricing.question: Which LLM API is cheapest in 2026?
models--pricing.answer: By input price per 1M tokens, the cheapest models in the table above are Llama 4 Scout ($0.08 in / $0.30 out), DeepSeek V4 Flash ($0.09 in / $0.18 out), Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 in / $0.50 out). The cheapest closed-weight API is Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10 input. The lowest output rate is DeepSeek V4 Flash at $0.18. Open-weight model prices come from third-party hosts and vary by provider. A low per-token rate is not always the cheapest task: check output price and how many tokens the model needs.

models--pricing.question: Do any AI models offer a free API tier in 2026?
models--pricing.answer: Yes. Several models including Llama 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Qwen3 offer free rate-limited API access. See the free models directory at /free-models for the full list with usage limits.

models--pricing.question: What is batch API pricing and how much can it save?
models--pricing.answer: Batch API pricing is an asynchronous processing mode offered by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google at 50% off standard rates. It is suitable for offline jobs such as embeddings, classification, and bulk summarization where results are not needed in real time.

models--pricing.question: How much does prompt caching reduce AI model costs?
models--pricing.answer: Cache hits on most Claude models cost 10% of the standard input rate, 5% on Claude Opus 5.5 and 2.5% on Claude Fable 5.1, per Anthropic's pricing page. OpenAI lists cached input at 10% of the input rate for GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna. For workloads with long repeated system prompts or documents, real costs can be 80 to 90% lower than the calculator's base estimate.
